question: Transform equation (1) into a straight line graph to determine $R_0$ and $\lambda$.
Form a suitable composite table containing all the necessary parameters to determine the approximate values of $R_0$ and $\lambda$ graphically.
Use your graph to determine the approximate values of $R_0$ and $\lambda$.
From the graph, find the approximate value of $R$ when $t = 0.36\text{ seconds}$.

Hang two spiral springs of nearly the same elastic constants in series from a rigid support as shown in figure 1 with $M = 50\text{g}$. Displace the spring vertically downward through a small distance and gently release it. The spring performs simple harmonic oscillations. With the help of stop watch record the time for 20 complete oscillations. Find the time period $T$. Evaluate $T^2$. Repeat the experiment for five more different values of $M$ within the elastic limit.
i. Tabulate your readings.
ii. Plot a graph of $T^2$ against $M$. Find the slope $S$ of the graph.
iii. If $T = 2\pi \sqrt{\frac{M}{2k}}$, Use your slope to find the value of $k$.
iv. State two precautions taken to ensure accurate results.

Use the diagram in figure 2.1 to carry out the following instructions. For the ray PQRS, the angle of incidence is $i$ and the angle of emergence is $\theta$.
i. Trace the outline of a triangular glass prism ABC. Set the angle of incidence $i = 25^\circ$. With the help of the optical pins, find the angle of emergence $\theta$.
ii. Measure and record the corresponding angle marked 'a'. Evaluate $\sin\theta$ and $\sin a$.
iii. Repeat the experiments with $i = 30^\circ, 40^\circ, 45^\circ, 50^\circ$ and $55^\circ$ respectively.
iv. Prepare a composite table for your readings. Plot a graph of $\sin a$ against $\sin\theta$. Find the slope $S$ of the graph and evaluate $S^{-1}$.
v. State two precautions taken to ensure accurate results.
